bands.1:
"The plan has three parts," says the Architect. "First, we climb. Second, we open Maxx's office. Third, we free Girderoo. In conclusion, wear warm socks."

At midnight, you all climb the icy ladders.

A gold drone swings round the tower. Gus shakes his jar of dandruff. Now the drone sees only snow.

"Why did the blueprint go to the doctor?" asks Mo. "It felt blue!"

At the top is Maxx World. It is rows of tiny gold cages.

Zed types MAXXISGREAT. Beep. He types ILOVEME. Beep. He types GORGEOUSME.

BUZZ! The screen says, "KEYPAD LOCKED."

"Part two is broken," says the Architect.

Then you see a small hatch on the back of the office. It has four bolts. They say THIRD, IN CONCLUSION, FIRST and SECOND.

"You built this office," you say. "It opens the way you talk."

You open the bolts in order. First. Second. Third. In conclusion. The hatch swings open.

Inside are the blueprints. They show a theme park made of cages. A statue of Maxx is drawn taller than the tower.

"He always draws himself taller," says Wren quietly.

"It has a way in," says the Architect. "It has no way out. In conclusion, it's a prison."

You roll up the blueprints. That's the proof.

Wren opens the cages. Girderoo jumps into the Architect's arms.

But the keypad is still buzzing. Goldies climb up every ladder.

"Always build a way out," says the Architect.

Girderoo thumps one plank. Every ladder folds flat into a giant slide. The Goldies whoosh down into the snow.

On the boat, you open the last blueprint. In the middle is a tank as big as a lake. It says, "THE BIG ONE. Catch her live on opening night!"

Only Old Glimmer, the giant glowing ray, could fit in that tank.

The Architect rolls up the blueprint. "In conclusion," she says, "we must beat him to opening night."
bands.2:
"The plan has three parts," says the Architect. "First, we climb the tower while the Goldies sleep. Second, we open Maxx's site office. Third, we free Girderoo. In conclusion, wear warm socks."

You have won her badge, and now she is on your side.

Indi hands out disguises: orange vests that say "TOTALLY REAL BUILDERS" and hard hats that are really saucepans. Mo's hard hat is a colander.

At midnight, the crew starts to climb. The ladders are icy.

A MaxxCam drone swings round the tower. Gus opens a jar of white flakes. "The Dandruff Blizzard," he whispers. "Two whole years of my dandruff." One shake, and the drone films nothing but snow.

"Why did the blueprint go to the doctor?" pants Mo. "It was feeling blue!"

At the top, behind a gold fence, Maxx World is half built. Rows of tiny gold cages stand in the snow.

The site office is a gold shipping container. Zed types MAXXISGREAT. Buzz. He types ILOVEME. Buzz. He types GORGEOUSME.

The keypad squeals. "THREE WRONG GUESSES. KEYPAD LOCKED."

Far below, a light comes on in the Goldies' hut.

"Second," says the Architect. "Second..." Her plan has no next part.

Then you spot a hatch at the back of the office. It has four bolts, stamped THIRD, IN CONCLUSION, FIRST and SECOND.

"You designed this office," you say. "So it opens the way you talk."

The Architect slides the bolts back in order. First. Second. Third. In conclusion. The hatch swings open.

Inside are her stolen blueprints. They show a theme park made of cages, with a "Cage Coaster" and a booth that says "SELFIE WITH A SAD CREATURE: $50." At the front is a statue of Maxx, taller than the tower.

"He always draws himself taller," says Wren, so quietly that only you hear.

"It has an entrance and no exit," says the Architect. "In conclusion, it's a prison with a gift shop."

You roll up the blueprints. That's the proof.

Wren and the Architect open the cages. Girderoo leaps into the Architect's arms.

Then floodlights blaze. Goldies swarm up every ladder.

"Always build a way out," says the Architect.

Girderoo thumps one plank. Every ladder folds flat into a giant slide, and the Goldies whoosh down into the snow.

On the boat, you unroll the last blueprint. In the middle is a tank as wide as a lake. It says, "STAR ATTRACTION: THE BIG ONE. Catch her live on opening night!"

Only one Creature could fill a tank that big: Old Glimmer, the great glowing ray from the sea stories.

The Architect rolls the blueprint up tightly. "In conclusion," she says, "we have until opening night."
bands.3:
"The plan has three parts," says the Architect, unrolling a blueprint across Mo's kitchen bench, right on top of the porridge. "First, we climb the north tower while the Goldies sleep. Second, we open Maxx's site office and take back my drawings. Third, we free Girderoo and every Creature with him. In conclusion, wear warm socks."

You have won her badge, and the builder of Scaffold Peaks is finally on your side.

Indi hands out disguises: orange vests that say "TOTALLY REAL BUILDERS" and hard hats that are really upside-down saucepans. Mo's hard hat is a colander.

At midnight, the crew starts to climb. The ladders are slick with ice.

Halfway up, a MaxxCam drone swings round the tower, its red light blinking. Gus opens a jar of white flakes, two years of his own dandruff, and gives it one shake. The flurry swirls into the lens, and the drone films nothing but snow.

"Why did the blueprint go to the doctor?" pants Mo. "It was feeling blue!"

Across the valley, a Chorrawong groans back at him.

Behind the gold fence at the top, Maxx World is half built. Rows of tiny gold cages stand in the snow, each with a cheerful sign that says "HAPPY HOME".

The site office is a gold shipping container. Zed types MAXXISGREAT. Buzz. He types ILOVEME. Buzz. Then, very confidently, he types GORGEOUSME.

The keypad gives a long squeal. "THREE WRONG GUESSES. KEYPAD LOCKED. SECURITY INFORMED."

Far below, a light comes on in the Goldies' hut.

"Second," says the Architect, and stops. "Second..." For the first time since you met her, her plan has no next part.

Then you spot a square hatch low in the back wall. It is held shut by four steel bolts, stamped THIRD, IN CONCLUSION, FIRST and SECOND.

"You designed this office before he locked you out," you say. "So it opens the way you talk."

The Architect looks at you, then at the bolts. First. Second. Third. In conclusion. Each bolt slides back with a clunk, and the hatch swings open.

Inside, her stolen blueprints are pinned to the wall. They show a theme park made of cages, with a "Cage Coaster", a gift shop and a booth that says "SELFIE WITH A SAD CREATURE: $50. SADDER CREATURE: $80." At the front stands a statue of Maxx, taller than the tower.

"He always draws himself taller," says Wren, so quietly that only you hear.

The Architect traces the plan with one finger. "It has an entrance and no exit. In conclusion, it's a prison with a gift shop."

You roll up the blueprints and tuck them inside your vest. That's the proof.

Wren and the Architect open the cages: Tracewhisks, Topsittles, a Heddrake and a jar of shivering Stagglets. In the last cage sits Girderoo, under a sign that says "MASCOT. PRACTISE SMILING." He leaps into the Architect's arms.

Then the floodlights blaze, and Goldies swarm up every ladder at once.

"First rule of building," says the Architect. "Always build a way out."

Girderoo thumps one plank. With a long clatter, every ladder folds flat into a wooden slide, and the Goldies whoosh down it into a soft snowdrift.

Back on the Soggy Biscuit, you unroll the last blueprint. In the centre of Maxx World is a tank as wide as a lake. Its gold label says, "STAR ATTRACTION: THE BIG ONE. Catch her live on opening night!"

Only one Creature in the old sea stories could fill a tank that big: Old Glimmer, the great glowing ray.

The Architect measures it twice, then rolls the blueprint up very tightly. "In conclusion," she says, "we have until opening night."
bands.4:
The Architect explains the plan the way she explains everything: in order, with one finger raised. "First, we climb the north tower while the Goldies sleep. Second, we open Maxx's site office and take back the drawings he stole from me. Third, we free Girderoo and every Creature with him." She lowers the finger. "In conclusion, wear warm socks."

Yesterday she would not let you set foot on her scaffolds. Tonight her badge is pinned to your jacket, and she has drawn the whole route across Mo's kitchen bench in pencil, right through the pickled-onion porridge.

"A speedrun with a proper map," says Zed. "Nothing can go wrong."

Indi hands out orange vests cut from old life jackets, each stencilled "TOTALLY REAL BUILDERS", and hard hats that are really saucepans turned upside down. Mo's is a colander. "For air flow," says Indi, not quite meeting his eyes.

At midnight, the crew starts to climb. The rungs are glazed with ice, and the wind finds every gap in every vest. Halfway up, a MaxxCam drone swings round the tower, its red light blinking. Gus unscrews a jar of white flakes, two years of his own dandruff, and gives it one patient shake. The flurry swirls into the lens, and the drone hovers there, faithfully filming the dullest snowstorm in history.

"Why did the blueprint go to the doctor?" pants Mo. "It was feeling blue."

Somewhere across the valley, a Chorrawong groans back at him.

Behind the gold fence at the top, Maxx World is half built. Rows of tiny gold cages stand in the snow, each with a cheerful sign that says "HAPPY HOME". Every sign faces the gate, where the visitors will stand. Not one of them faces the cages.

The site office is a gold shipping container with a keypad by the door. Zed cracks his knuckles and types MAXXISGREAT. An angry buzz. He tries ILOVEME. Another buzz. With the confidence of someone who has never once been wrong about Maxx, he types GORGEOUSME.

The keypad gives a long, flat squeal. "THREE WRONG GUESSES," says the screen. "KEYPAD LOCKED. SECURITY INFORMED."

Far below, a light comes on in the Goldies' hut.

The Architect stares at the keypad as if it has insulted her drawings. "Second," she says, and stops. "Second..." For the first time since you met her, there is no next part.

You are not looking at the keypad, though. Low in the back wall of the container sits a square hatch, held shut by four steel bolts, and each bolt has a word stamped into it: THIRD, IN CONCLUSION, FIRST, SECOND.

"You designed this office," you say, "before he locked you out."

"Every building I draw has a second way in," she says slowly. "Maxx never reads past page one."

"Then it opens the way you talk."

She looks at you, then at the bolts. First. Second. Third. In conclusion. Each one slides back with a clunk, and the hatch swings open as neatly as a sentence ending.

Inside, her stolen blueprints are pinned to the wall. They show a theme park built entirely of cages: a "Cage Coaster" rattling past the enclosures, a gift shop of plush Maxxes, and beside the gate a booth labelled "SELFIE WITH A SAD CREATURE: $50. SADDER CREATURE: $80." At the front stands a statue of Maxx, drawn taller than the tower it stands on.

"He always draws himself taller," says Wren, so quietly that only you hear.

The Architect traces the plan with one finger, from the entrance all the way round and back to the entrance. She does it twice. "In conclusion," she says, "it's a prison with a gift shop."

You roll the blueprints up and slide them inside your vest.

Out the back, Wren and the Architect open the cages one by one: Tracewhisks, Topsittles, a Heddrake with its tail tucked under its chin, a jar of shivering Stagglets. In the last cage sits Girderoo, hard hat crooked, under a sign that says "MASCOT. PRACTISE SMILING." He does not smile. He leaps into the Architect's arms and thumps her chin with his nose until she laughs.

Then the floodlights blaze, and Goldies come swarming up every ladder at once.

"First rule of building," says the Architect. "Always build a way out."

Girderoo hops onto the scaffold and thumps one plank. With a long, rattling clatter, every ladder below folds flat into a wooden slide, and the Goldies whoosh down it one after another into a deep, soft snowdrift. The crew follows, Creatures held tight.

Back on the Soggy Biscuit, you unroll the last blueprint. In the centre of Maxx World is a tank as wide as a lake, labelled in gold pen: "STAR ATTRACTION: THE BIG ONE. Catch her live on opening night!" No fish needs a lake. Only one Creature in the old sea stories could fill it: Old Glimmer, the great glowing ray.

The Architect measures the tank twice. Then she rolls the blueprint up very tightly.

"In conclusion," she says, "we have until opening night."
